checks.note: signUpload presigns PUT binding only bucket/key/contentType (no contentLength or conditional header), and persistConfirmed records head.contentLength() plus the client-declared checksum without storing head.eTag() or a version id, so nothing detects a re-PUT within uploadTtlSeconds after confirm; all later reads (signDownload, findActiveObject, assertOwnership) trust the stale FileStorageObject row. The caveat doesn't save it: the TTL must be >0 for the flow to work, and S3 versioning/object-lock still serve the newest PUT as current.

In-file mechanics are real: signUpload persists nothing, quota uses sumSizeBytesByOwnerId (confirmed rows only), and confirmUpload's StorageValidationException/QuotaExceededException paths never deleteObject, orphaning the S3 object. But the finding's verification caveat — absence of an S3 lifecycle rule in infrastructure/terraform (and any upstream rate limit on /api/storage/sign/upload) — cannot be checked from this file, so "never garbage-collected / unbounded cost" is not settled.

persistConfirmed stores request.checksum() and resolveOriginalFilename returns request.originalFilename() raw; validationChain.validate runs only in signUpload on the synthesized entity+"."+extension filename, and formatChecksum prefixes "sha256:" onto the uncompared string surfaced via findActiveObject. Caveat: the migration's column lengths and any Content-Disposition consumers are not in the provided file, so the unbounded-length and header-injection consequences remain unverified downstream.

softDelete does throw AuthorizationException(MISSING_RIGHTS) for an existing active key with a non-matching createdBy, versus StorageObjectNotFoundException when no active row exists — the differential exception the finding describes is real. But the finding's verification step (that AuthorizationException maps to a 403, not 404, in the HTTP layer) requires the exception handler/@ControllerAdvice, which is not in the provided file.

Confirmed in-file that softDelete authorizes on fso.getCreatedBy() vs currentUserLogin while signDownload/reconfirm/assertOwnership all use fso.getOwnerId() (set from securityUtil.requireCurrentBusinessId() in persistConfirmed). But the consequence depends on whether createdBy (set by an unshown AuditorAware; never assigned in this file) can diverge from the caller's login — e.g. via login/email change — which requires the AuditorAware, SecurityUtil, and FileStorageObject entity code not provided.
